title: Generating random numbers using Mersenne Twister
recap: Raw engine output spans a huge range, so a distribution converts it into the range you actually want. std::uniform_int_distribution produces every value in a closed range with equal probability.
Reuse one distribution object across draws instead of constructing a new one each time. Avoid shaping raw output with the remainder operator, which biases the result toward smaller values.
objectives: Implement rollTotal from its behavioral contract.
Practice the lesson construct by writing the control flow yourself.
Handle multiple inputs and edge cases without hard-coded example answers.
warnings: The examples are not the whole test suite; implement the general behavior.
Do not edit the test drivers. Only the supplied public function signatures are fixed.
Console output and exact source tokens are not graded.
challenge: Implement rollTotal. Seed a fresh std::mt19937 with seed, then draw rolls values with std::uniform_int_distribution<int>{1, 4}. Return their sum, not printed roll lines. Return 0 for rolls <= 0. Draw exactly once per roll and reset the engine on each function call. The four-sided range is intentionally a power of two; tested roll counts are at most 1000.
hints: Construct the engine and the distribution once, before the loop.
Call die(generator) once per iteration and add its result.
Return the total; do not use modulo to replace the specified distribution.
